newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to name winner of bank asset sale on July 9.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to name winner of bank asset sale on July 9.

text.p: Mexico will announce on July 9 the result of its fledgling attempt to sell off bank assets taken by the government during the country's economic crisis, lead bank Banco GBM-Atlantico said on Wednesday.

The 150 million peso sale is the first of what is expected to eventually be a 300 million peso auction process. Via its sale vehicle, known as Valuation and Sale of Assets, the government hopes to shed most of the shaky loans it took off banks in 1995 and 1996.
The bidding process formally begins on June 13, which is the last day for acquiring brochures on the assets for sale.
GBM-Atlantico and Bankers Trust Co are lead and co-lead of manager of the auction process.
The first package up for sale is made up of 36 credits, of which 32 are loans that are still current, they said.
Bidders can either seek to acquire the entire portfolio, or take a 55 percent stake of the shares in a special-purpose vehicle known as the Business Recovery Fund (SRE).
The other 45 percent of shares will be held by the government's Bank Insurance Fund, Fobaproa, which will be a sleeping partner in the SRE.
